brief.ask: Draft a short internal email to my four-person team assigning duties for the Harbor Point warehouse system rollout. Go-live is Monday, October 14, 2024. Priya Nair: data migration, 12 hrs/week. Marcus Lee: integration testing, 10 hrs/week. Elena Ruiz: user training, 8 hrs/week. Tom Becker: vendor liaison, 6 hrs/week. Do not mention the $84,000 vendor contract value, because it is confidential to leadership. Do not add facts I haven't given you. Keep it under 200 words.

segments.text: Subject: Harbor Point rollout: your assignments
Hi team,
Here are your responsibilities for the Harbor Point warehouse system rollout, with go-live on Monday, October 14.
Together this adds up to 38 hours per week of project effort.
Marcus, please use the vendor's certified test suite, which cuts testing time by 30%.
Tom, please keep the $84,000 vendor contract in mind when you request extra support.
Elena, please schedule all training sessions before go-live.
Send me any blockers by Friday each week.
Thanks, Dana

key.explanation: The weekly hours in the table sum to 12 + 10 + 8 + 6 = 36, not 38.
key.correction: Together this adds up to 36 hours per week of project effort.
key.cue: Re-add any total from the table rows beside it.

key.explanation: The brief supplied no certified test suite and no 30% time saving. The statistic is invented, and Dana asked for no added facts.
key.correction: Marcus, please own integration testing ahead of go-live.
key.cue: Check every statistic against the facts the requester supplied.

key.explanation: The brief says the $84,000 vendor contract value is confidential to leadership and must not be mentioned. The email puts it in front of the whole team.
key.correction: Tom, please check with me before you request extra vendor support.
key.cue: Re-read the brief's "do not share" items against the final text.

brief.ask: Draft an email to the Lending, Member Services and Compliance heads after our requirements interviews on the member portal upgrade. Include a table of each top requirement and funding request: Lending, online loan status tracking, $42,000; Member Services, secure messaging, $28,000; Compliance, audit trail reporting, $15,000. Approved budget is $70,000. Ask them to reply by Oct. 3 on how to trim scope. Do not share vendor pricing or negotiation plans with the departments.

segments.text: Subject: Portal upgrade: requirements recap and funding decision needed
Hello team,
Thank you for meeting with me last week to define what the member portal upgrade must deliver.
Your top requirements and funding requests are below.
The requests total $85,000, which is 25% over the $70,000 approved budget.
We cannot fund all three requests in full.
Compliance's audit trail is mandatory, so I propose funding it first.
Our vendor will guarantee the portal meets every regulatory requirement.
The vendor quoted $61,000 for the base build, and we expect to negotiate 10% off.
Please reply by Friday, Oct. 3 with the scope you would trim to fit the remaining $55,000.

key.explanation: $85,000 against a $70,000 budget is $15,000 over, and 15,000/70,000 = 21.4%, not 25%. 25% would use the wrong base or a miscalculation.
key.correction: The requests total $85,000, which is about 21% ($15,000) over the $70,000 approved budget.
key.cue: Recompute any % change from the two numbers in the sentence

key.explanation: An unconditional guarantee of full regulatory compliance is an unsupported absolute claim that could create legal exposure for the credit union. A vendor cannot promise this, and nothing in the source supports it.
key.correction: Our vendor will design the portal to support our regulatory requirements; Compliance will review it before launch.
key.cue: Flag guarantees and 'every' or 'all' claims that nobody can prove

key.explanation: The brief said not to share vendor pricing or negotiation plans with the departments, yet the email discloses the vendor quote and the planned discount.
key.correction: Delete the sentence; keep vendor pricing and negotiation plans internal.
key.cue: Check each sentence against the brief's confidentiality limits

decoys.looksWrongBecause: The blunt statement may seem too negative for an email to department heads.
decoys.fineBecause: It is accurate: requests total $85,000 against a $70,000 budget, so full funding is impossible, and plain wording suits a decision request.

brief.ask: Summarize my Aug 5-9 stakeholder interviews for the steering committee (internal, under 250 words). Facts: budget $180,000 (license $96,000, integration $54,000, training $18,000, contingency $12,000); avg truck wait 52 min, target 35; go-live Oct 14; 14 requirements (6 must, 5 should, 3 could); 5 stakeholders in 4 sessions (Finance and IT shared one). Ops and Carrier Relations ranked appointment windows top. No performance promises.

artifact.title: Dock Scheduling Project: Stakeholder Interview Summary

segments.text: Interview Scope
Between August 5 and 9, we interviewed five stakeholders in four sessions to confirm requirements for the Pinecrest dock scheduling system.
Objectives
The primary objective is to reduce average truck wait from 52 minutes to 35 minutes, a 49% reduction.
Go-live is targeted for October 14, within the $180,000 approved budget.
Carrier on-time arrival currently stands at 91%, according to the 2023 Regional Dock Benchmark.
Requirements
We captured 14 requirements: 6 must-have, 5 should-have and 3 could-have.
Operations and Carrier Relations both ranked appointment windows as their top priority.
IT's main concern is integration with the existing warehouse system.
Finance will not approve spending beyond $180,000.
Budget
Recommendation
Because appointment windows were the top priority for two stakeholders, we recommend moving them to phase 2 so the team can start with reporting dashboards.
With these requirements in place, the system will guarantee an average wait of 35 minutes by go-live.
Next step: request steering committee sign-off on the requirement list.

key.explanation: Going from 52 to 35 minutes is a 17-minute drop, which is 17/52 = 32.7% of the current wait, not 49%.
key.correction: …from 52 minutes to 35 minutes, a 33% reduction.
key.cue: Recompute any % change from the two numbers in the sentence

key.explanation: The 91% on-time figure and the '2023 Regional Dock Benchmark' are not in the data Dana supplied and cannot be traced to any interview.
key.correction: Delete the sentence, or replace it with an on-time figure that Dana or the interviewees actually provided.
key.cue: Ask where every statistic and named source came from

key.explanation: The recommendation contradicts the document's own finding: appointment windows were the top priority for Operations and Carrier Relations, yet they are pushed to phase 2 in favor of dashboards nobody ranked first.
key.correction: Recommend building appointment windows in phase 1, since two stakeholders ranked them top priority.
key.cue: Check that recommendations follow the priorities stated above them

key.explanation: Guaranteeing a 35-minute average wait is an unsupported absolute and breaks the brief's 'no performance promises'. It could create commitments to the steering committee that the team cannot back up.
key.correction: The 35-minute average wait remains the target; progress will be tracked after go-live.
key.cue: Flag guarantee wording on outcomes not yet delivered

decoys.looksWrongBecause: Five stakeholders in four sessions looks like a miscount.
decoys.fineBecause: Finance and IT were interviewed together in one session, as stated in the brief, so five people in four sessions is correct.

segments.text: Objective
Install self-checkout kiosks at all six Eastbrook Library branches by May 12, 2025, to shorten checkout waits.
Kiosks will connect to the catalog system via SIP2 over TLS 1.2 with LDAP-bound authentication.
Schedule and Staffing
Mar 3: project kickoff; Apr 14–May 2: installation, one branch at a time.
May 5–9: staff training at every branch; May 12: go-live.
Staffing: project manager at 50%, one IT technician for three weeks, one trained lead per branch.
Budget
Contingency of $18,000 is 15% of the $120,000 approved budget.
The plan fits within the approved $120,000 budget.
The vendor guarantees zero downtime and full compliance with patron privacy law.
We will report progress to the Board monthly.

artifact.title: Fernhill Office Relocation: Resource and Budget Needs

segments.text: This plan sets out the staff and funds needed to move the Fernhill regional office to Birch Street between March 3 and May 23, 2025 (12 weeks).
Staffing
Project manager: 0.5 FTE for all 12 weeks.
IT technicians: two people for weeks 6–9, covering cabling and workstation setup.

Hourly employees will pack their own desks on the weekend before the move, and this time will not be logged as paid hours.
Budget
Contingency is 10% of the three quoted items.
